fields.label: MTU
fields.help: Packet size on the tunnel interface.
fields.breaks_when_wrong: Too large: the handshake succeeds, ping succeeds, and TCP hangs on the first full-size frame.

fields.label: PersistentKeepalive
fields.help: How often the client speaks even when idle, to keep NAT mappings alive.
fields.breaks_when_wrong: Behind NAT the mapping expires after about two minutes and the tunnel goes one-way until the client sends again.

fields.label: DNS server
fields.help: Pushed to the client only when set; only useful with a full-tunnel profile.
fields.breaks_when_wrong: A malformed address makes wg-quick fail to bring the interface up at all.

fields.label: Routing table
fields.help: wg-quick's Table= setting for this config.
fields.breaks_when_wrong: off means the AllowedIPs selection is written into the file but never actually routed.

fields.label: DNS handling
fields.help: What happens to the client's resolver while the tunnel is up.
fields.breaks_when_wrong: Tunnel DNS on a split-tunnel profile leaks every lookup through the tunnel.

fields.label: Server public key
fields.help: Identifies this host to the client; public by design.

fields.label: Preshared key
fields.help: Optional second secret; the same value must be present on both ends.
fields.breaks_when_wrong: A mismatch fails the handshake with no error message on either side.

fields.label: Destinations
fields.help: What the client routes into the tunnel; the server-side /32 is derived from the same selection.
fields.breaks_when_wrong: The single most common failure: the destination list lands on the wrong side and the tunnel connects while nothing works.

fields.label: IPv4 forwarding
fields.help: net.ipv4.ip_forward on this host; global, not per tunnel.
fields.breaks_when_wrong: The tunnel comes up and this host refuses to pass packets through it.

recommendations.text: Routing to the LAN needs masquerade for 172.16.0.0/24 → bridge0. It is <state>.
Reaching anything behind this host needs net.ipv4.ip_forward. It is <state>.
Keepalive 0 disables it: behind NAT the tunnel will go one-way when idle.
Client DNS will be rewritten while the tunnel is up.
MTU above 1420 rarely survives the WireGuard encapsulation overhead on this path.
MTU below 1320 wastes bandwidth; only double-encapsulated paths need it.
Forwarding is enabled host-wide, not per tunnel: every routed interface on this host is affected.
